5712.title: [skia-sync] Merge upstream chrome/m158 bug fixes
5712.body:
[M158] Sync Vulkan synchronization and displacement fixes (#5712)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/451
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5715
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/600a5886625b49b5955f23c1ab1e45b68933d0dd...c8c6d08ae1ce0578c4e440dd2fe7449460f513f5

Bring the chrome/m158 Vulkan fence-wait and displacement-precision fixes
into release/4.158.x. Keep package versions and the public API unchanged;
this is a same-milestone native correctness update.

~~ Propagate synchronous Vulkan fence-wait failures in native submission ~~

Native Ganesh previously returned queue submission success even when the
subsequent synchronous vkWaitForFences failed. The void forceSync()
helper could not propagate that wait failure to the submission result.

The native update makes forceSync() return a bool and combines the wait
result with queue submission success when CPU synchronization is
requested. An absent fence is already complete; an actual wait succeeds
only on VK_SUCCESS. Retain the VK_TIMEOUT retry for signal-interrupted
drivers, submission cleanup and asynchronous submission behavior.

This corrects native Ganesh's failure reporting without adding a managed
result: GRContext.Submit remains void, and the C bridge and managed
signatures are unchanged.

~~ Align displacement offsets with fp32 filter bounds ~~

Half-precision displacement scale and offset arithmetic could round
differently from the fp32 filter-bounds calculation and sample a
different location. Use float2 for the scale uniform, helper parameter
and displacement vector so offset arithmetic matches the bounds
precision. Keep displacement colors and channel selectors at half
precision; both generated shader variants follow the updated helper.

~~ Record landed native ancestry without changing reviewed sources ~~

Advance externals/skia and its Component Governance registration from
600a5886625b49b5955f23c1ab1e45b68933d0dd to actual native merge
c8c6d08ae1ce0578c4e440dd2fe7449460f513f5. Record exact upstream commit
2d58f195f426c41bd856208ddb85ea8f93c88295 while retaining milestone 158
and upstream_ref chrome/m158.

The dependent repin in #5715 changes the gitlink and matching manifest
hash from reviewed head 038363ac1db8b60d2455922f6af6558e34eabfd3 to the
landed merge. That merge has two parents, directly includes the reviewed
head and shares its exact tree,
e4a986dde9cafacbbdddd92b617f753ea0293ea5. Preserve this ancestry so
future syncs can identify already integrated upstream commits.

The source review found the complete seven-file native delta identical
to the upstream fixes, with 72 non-interop fork patches and 106 interop
files preserved and DEPS unchanged. Independent regeneration matched the
five managed binding directories. The parent diff changes the gitlink
and manifest provenance, not wrappers, generated bindings, tests,
dependency versions or package/ABI version inputs.

Tree equality preserves the reviewed native content; it is not a new
runtime test run or proof of affected-device Vulkan failure-path and
displacement-boundary coverage.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

5408.title: Enable CA5394 for shipped code and use a CSPRNG for the HashCode seed
5408.body:
* Enable CA5394 (insecure randomness) as an error for shipping code

CA5394 is disabled by default, so nothing would catch a new use of
System.Random in the shipping assemblies. Enable it as an error for
binding/ and source/ with a path-scoped .editorconfig section, so that
any new use has to be justified.

The only existing hit in shipping code is the hash seed in
Binding.Shared/HashCode.cs (compiled into both SkiaSharp.dll and
HarfBuzzSharp.dll). It only randomizes hash codes between processes and
is not security sensitive, so suppress it with a comment instead of
changing behavior.

Notes:

* Samples, tests and benchmarks are not covered. They use System.Random
  for deterministic or throwaway data (21 call sites in the Gallery
  sample, the tests and the benchmarks would otherwise be reported, and
  the Gallery projects treat warnings as errors).
* The rule is only reported for target frameworks where the SDK's bundled
  analyzers run: net5.0 and later, including the platform TFMs.
  netstandard2.0/2.1, net462 and net48 are not analyzed unless
  EnableNETAnalyzers=true is set. All TFMs compile the same files, so the
  other TFMs still catch new uses in shared code.
* The severity is error instead of warning on purpose: only binding/ has
  TreatWarningsAsErrors=true, so a warning would not fail the build in
  source/.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Document the CA5394 rule for contributors

Mention in the file conventions that System.Random cannot be used in
binding/ and source/ without a justification, and what to do instead,
since the build now reports it as an error there.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Seed HashCode from the OS CSPRNG instead of suppressing CA5394

The only System.Random use in shipped code was the per-process seed of
the HashCode polyfill in Binding.Shared/HashCode.cs, which is compiled
into both SkiaSharp.dll and HarfBuzzSharp.dll. The previous commit
suppressed CA5394 for it. Fix it instead, so that the new CA5394 guard
has no exceptions in shipped code.

The polyfill was copied from dotnet/runtime, where the seed comes from
the OS CSPRNG (Interop.GetRandomBytes), and Microsoft.Bcl.HashCode, the
official downlevel polyfill of System.HashCode, generates it with
RandomNumberGenerator. The copy used new Random ().Next () instead,
which is weaker:

* Random.Next () returns [0, int.MaxValue), so the seed only had 31 bits.
* On .NET Framework the parameterless Random constructor is seeded from
  the system clock (net462, net48, and netstandard2.0 assemblies running
  there).

Use RandomNumberGenerator.Create () and GetBytes, like
Microsoft.Bcl.HashCode does. It exists on all of our target frameworks
(netstandard2.0/2.1, net462/net48 and net6.0+, including the platform
TFMs), so no #if is needed. Hash codes are still randomized per process
and stable within a process.

The cost is that the first use of HashCode in a process now loads
System.Security.Cryptography and takes about 2 ms instead of 0.3 ms
(measured on net10.0, macOS arm64).

Also remove the references to HashCode.cs as the example of a justified
suppression from the .editorconfig comment and api-design.md, since
there is no suppression anymore.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Ignore CA5394 explicitly for code that is not shipped

CA5394 is disabled by default, so the samples, tests, benchmarks and
utils are not reported today. Say so explicitly, so that it also holds
if the rule gets enabled more broadly: AnalysisMode=All, for instance,
reports 21 call sites there. They are all seeded or throwaway uses of
Random (the day-seeded shuffle and the decorative dots in the Gallery,
buffers in the tests, input data in the benchmarks), where a CSPRNG
would be a regression.

The shipped code, the NuGet packages built from binding/ and source/,
keeps CA5394 as an error. Together the two sections cover all the C# in
the repository (outside of the externals submodule).

Verified with temporary files: a new System.Random use in binding/ or
source/ fails the build on the target frameworks where the SDK
analyzers run (net6.0 and later), the same use in utils/ is not
reported even with AnalysisMode=All, and in a directory that matches
neither section it is reported by AnalysisMode=All, so the exemption is
what silences it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Move the CA5394 settings to nested .editorconfig files

The root .editorconfig is in the global include of
scripts/infra/caching/repo-deps.json, so it is part of the cache key of
every native job. Editing it made CI think that the native inputs had
changed:

* The Azure native jobs all had a cache miss and rebuilt (636
  agent-minutes in the Native stages of the PR build, against 77 for a
  docs-only PR build).
* The benchmark-source workflow built libSkiaSharp from source on every
  OS, which currently fails on Windows because the runner image has no
  Spectre-mitigated MSVC libraries (mono/SkiaSharp#5321 is fixing that).

Put the error severity in binding/.editorconfig (which already exists)
and in a new source/.editorconfig instead. Neither file is part of the
native cache keys, so the keys are the same as the ones for the base
commit again, and repo-deps.py validate accepts the new file. A new
System.Random use in binding/ or source/ is still an error on the target
frameworks where the SDK analyzers run (net6.0 and later), and the code
that is not shipped keeps the default, which is that the rule is
disabled.

The explicit "none" for samples, tests, benchmarks and utils goes away.
It only made a difference if the rule is enabled more broadly
(AnalysisMode=All reports 21 call sites there), which nothing does
today.

Update the note in api-design.md to point at the new files.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

5669.title: [M158] Adopt upstream GPU correctness fixes
5669.body:
[M158] Adopt upstream GPU correctness fixes (#5669)

Context: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/439
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5675
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1671411
Changes: https://github.com/google/skia/compare/75584a96108b2bf0b1c74b0536126fa4917b64a8...361c8326695a06b7492fb6eeeff803c0c92a2447

Adopt the merged m158 GPU bug fixes without a milestone or package-version
transition. Update the native gitlink and Component Governance identities;
the companion native PR carries the implementation changes.

~~ Respect affected ARM Vulkan device-loss teardown timing ~~

Some Mali drivers report idle completion before device teardown is safe.
Adopt the Ganesh and Graphite workaround that adds a 1 ms delay on the
relevant loss paths for ARM proprietary drivers from 42.0 through versions
below 56.0, rather than delaying ordinary successful submissions.

~~ Preserve hairline cap scale under reflected transforms ~~

A negative determinant previously selected a local-space unit outset for
zero-length square-capped hairlines, allowing reflected scales to enlarge
the cap. Adopt the signed inverse-determinant calculation and finite-result
guard for singular matrices and overflow.

~~ Select text-atlas samplers despite interpolation imprecision ~~

Ganesh's flat-varying hint is not a guarantee. Adopt rounding before the
integer sampler-index comparison in ordinary and LCD atlas lookups so
interpolation error does not select the wrong atlas.

~~ Bound Graphite clip recording within a render pass ~~

Account for effective undrawn clip elements when deciding to flush.
Because flushing resets clip recording, reject and log a draw whose clips
cannot fit a fresh pass instead of overflowing the pass structures.
The native update includes DeviceTestClipRenderStepLimits.

~~ Pin the actual native merge without changing the reviewed tree ~~

Pin mono/skia merge 7329f82be5f66b326acdfadbc87a62793e6d6dba rather
than leaving the parent on the temporary reviewed branch head. Its two
parents include reviewed head 365bf08330f18bbe64c5e9f84f251262afe7f371,
and both commits have tree 3bf18d50473a78bcfe982206ef0810e825aad412.

Keep the gitlink and mono/skia commitHash aligned while recording exact
upstream commit 361c8326695a06b7492fb6eeeff803c0c92a2447 separately.
Retain chrome/m158 and milestone 158; no managed declarations or version
inputs change in this parent PR.

Build 1671411 succeeded for the pre-repin parent source, including the
single Mac Catalyst retry after an agent-side .NET setup permission error.
Independent regeneration matched the generated bindings. The repin changes
native commit identity, not its tree; affected-device Vulkan loss behavior
was not specifically established by the integration review.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

5554.title: Update HarfBuzz to 15.0.0 and complete script constants
5554.body:
Update HarfBuzz to 15.0.0 and complete script constants (#5554)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/419
Changes: https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/compare/36cb489cb02ce4b92099669ba9f9bea348eff93f...35f656a1a2bab548ea7f54a6dd3fba2b09680d14

Keep the native HarfBuzz revision, packaged library identity and managed
bindings aligned while adopting 15.0.0. Complete the manually maintained
Script constants without replacing their existing struct-based API.

~~ Align the native upgrade with its package identity ~~

Adopt HarfBuzz revision 35f656a1a2bab548ea7f54a6dd3fba2b09680d14
through mono/skia#419. The native companion updates DEPS and the GN source
inventory for the added headers and test sources, including the change
from OT/Layout/types.hh to hb-ot-dual.hh.

Pin externals/skia and its matching governance registration to native
commit fb69790c17977edad0142d277435ec5514dd0f2d. Record HarfBuzz
15.0.0 and its exact revision and version-header evidence in cgmanifest.

Advance the native SONAME from 0.61440.0 to 0.61500.0. Reset the
HarfBuzzSharp file and NativeAssets package versions from 14.4.0.300 to
15.0.0: a native version upgrade establishes a new revision-zero bucket,
rather than continuing the previous version's milestone servicing range.
Keep the HarfBuzzSharp assembly version at 1.0.0.0 and retain the m158
SkiaSharp product versions.

The rebased source passed the macOS ARM64 native build and unfiltered
net10.0 console solution, including existing shaping and subsetting tests.

~~ Regenerate the deprecated font-face setter import ~~

HarfBuzz moves hb_font_set_face from hb-font.h to hb-deprecated.h and marks
it deprecated in favor of hb_font_create. The binding configuration
already excludes hb-deprecated.h, so regeneration removes the unused
internal hb_font_set_face declarations and delegate path.

Do not restore the import by hand or widen deprecated-header generation:
Font(Face) already constructs fonts through hb_font_create, and this
removal does not remove a public managed member. The current-head
binding-generation determinism check passes after regeneration.

~~ Complete named scripts without changing the Script programming model ~~

The native script list advanced while Script.fields.cs remained manually
maintained. Regenerating interop alone cannot repair that gap:
hb_script_t deliberately maps to UInt32 with generation disabled because
HarfBuzzSharp exposes a custom Script struct, not a generated enum.

Add 30 documented static readonly fields: Jurchen, ProtoCuneiform and Seal
from the updated native list, plus 27 previously omitted constants.
Preserve the 149 existing field declarations and values. The resulting
179 named tag values match the HB_TAG entries in the selected native
hb-script-list.h.

Keep the struct's parsing, numeric conversions and horizontal-direction
lookup intact. Document the manual synchronization requirement beside the
generator mapping so future native updates do not mistake disabled enum
generation for complete script coverage.

Add a theory case for each new field, asserting its numeric tag,
ToString output, Parse result and successful TryParse round-trip against
the native-backed parser.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
